subject: Crestline: sudden throughput drop + elevated 5xx — exec war-room coordination
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@crestline.io>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>; Support <support@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@crestline.io>; Crestline Engineering <eng@crestline.io>
Date: 2026-12-08T22:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: service degradation - elevated 5xx and throughput collapse

Grace —

We started seeing a major regression in throughput around 18:10 PT. Our ingest QPS is the same but Redwood responses have collapsed (p50 latency up ~2x, p95 off the charts) and we’re seeing 5xx rate ~13% on production traffic. This is causing downstream backlog in our worker queue and impacting order processing.

We attached an error dump and a small sample of prefixes that reliably trigger the failure. Can Redwood confirm whether a model rollout or infra change was pushed in the last hour? We need a TTR estimate and an interim mitigation plan — restarting endpoints or routing to a secondary model would be acceptable short-term.

Attaching: error_dump_20261208.log (snippets), crestline-prefix-kv-sample.json

— Sanjay
Senior SRE, Crestline
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@crestline.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Support <support@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-08T22:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: service degradation - elevated 5xx and throughput collapse

Sanjay — thanks for the quick flag and the logs. We’ve engaged the stability team and are standing up an exec war-room now. Initial notes / asks: 

- Confirmed: no customer-facing model rollouts from Redwood in the last two hours (control plane audit attached).
- Immediate workstreams: 1) traffic routing failover 2) hotfix to NVMe-backed KV cache used by the prefix cache 3) telemetry deep-dive on memory/GC/KV eviction.
- Can you confirm whether you have a short list of high-priority prefixes we should failover first? The sample you sent is helpful.
- We’ll propose a temporary routing rule to send new requests for low-latency critical endpoints to a compatible model variant with slightly lower token throughput but stable latency. This will be a canary first then full cut-over if p95 improves.

War-room participants (invited): Marissa Cole (ENG lead, runtime), David Kim (Sales + customer liaison), Laura Bennett (Customer Success). I’ll coordinate exec updates; Marissa will lead technical triage.

War-room join: Slack channel GW-WARROOM-crestline (link: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/GW-WARROOM-crestline)
Jira: RED-9134 (we’ll update the ticket with postmortem actions)

I’ll send an exec brief to your leadership in 30m with current scope and TTR estimate.

— Grace
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>; David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Crestline Engineering <eng@crestline.io>
Date: 2026-12-08T23:01:00-08:00
Subject: [WAR-ROOM] Crestline throughput/5xx — immediate action items

Team — war-room kickoff (joining now). Short action list: 

1) Routing failover (Marissa, Eng infra): prepare traffic split to secondary model variant v2-compatible, target 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 15min windows. Goal: reduce p95 by 30% within first 30m.
2) KV cache investigation (Eng runtime pod): snapshot cache eviction rate and hotkey distribution; probe NVMe latency on nodes referenced in logs.
3) Telemetry (David): push a tight dashboard to Crestline exec with p50/p95, 5xx%, and queue depth. Link to dashboard will be posted in Slack.
4) Customer comms (Grace + Laura): draft an executive summary with user impact, interim mitigations, and ETA for full resolution. Target: initial exec summary to Crestline leadership in 30m.
5) Rollback/Restart plan (Marissa): if routing failover doesn’t lower 5xx within 45m, schedule controlled restart of the affected runtime pool during the 02:30 UTC maintenance window (notify Crestline).

Notes: attaching a quick runbook and the map of affected endpoints (Crestline-MAP.xlsx). I’ll post telemetry snapshots in the Slack channel as we get them.

— Marissa
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@crestline.io>; Priya Desai <priya.desai@crestline.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Support <support@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-09T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Crestline — executive update (interim mitigations in progress)

Sanjay / Priya —

Quick executive summary and current status (T+~16h since initial anomaly):

- Impact: elevated 5xx peaked at 13% yesterday evening; throughput for critical endpoints reduced by ~60% (order-ingest path). No data loss observed; backlog being processed but delayed.
- Actions taken: routing failover to variant v2 initiated (10% -> 60% in staged increments), NVMe-backed KV cache eviction tuning applied to 6 nodes, and an emergency GC patch deployed to the runtime pool.
- Early results: p95 latency decreased ~28% on canary traffic; 5xx rate on routed traffic dropped to ~2.1%. Overall system 5xx is trending down but still above SLOs.
- Next steps: complete full routing cut-over (target +2h), continue KV telemetry for 24h, and run an incident postmortem for root cause (likely a hotspot in prefix KV eviction combined with an unexpected GC tail).
- Customer commitment: we will provide a full RCA and remediation plan within 72 hours and share a compensatory credit proposal aligned with the contract.

We’ve attached the raw error dump and the endpoint map for your records. I’ll host a readout with Crestline execs at 16:00 PT if that works for your leadership — please confirm.

Thanks for your partnership and patience; we’ll continue to push updates in the Slack war-room and via the Jira ticket RED-9134.

— Grace
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
